summary: Six depth-investigator interim notes exist and all are reflected to varying degrees; none is wholly ignored. The two indexed vault source notes (Fan/minimizing-ucb, Dewolf/valid-prediction-intervals) are well used. The gaps are concentrated where an interim note carries a verbatim quote, a newly-fetched adversarial rule-out, or a specific number that the draft blands into a paraphrase. Highest-value: the draft demands 'the specific overlapping sentence' per the query yet paraphrases PGS's premise (the sentence candidate A's whole ownership rests on); it omits three primary sources the interim notes fetched specifically to harden NONE-FOUND residuals (Lee 2019 arXiv:1902.06720 for N5; Lu 2023 + Benechehab 2024 for N3; Ziomek/LB arXiv:2410.10384 for N7).

findings.location: Candidate A paragraph ('Candidate Contributions', ~line 102) and N6 section (~line 65). The draft says A is 'the first ... ANOVA-quantified falsification of PGS's own motivating premise' and that 'PGS fixes the surrogate and cannot produce a number for its effect [33]', but never quotes PGS's premise.
findings.issue: Candidate A's entire distinctiveness rests on falsifying PGS's specific motivating premise, and the query explicitly requires 'the specific overlapping sentence.' The draft paraphrases the premise ('that offline black-box optimization had neglected the search-strategy lever') instead of quoting the verbatim sentence the interim note extracted. Without the quote, the reason no prior paper owns candidate A's one sentence is asserted rather than shown.
findings.evidence: interim-report-optimizer-reversal-unearned-and-candidate-a-credit gives the verbatim PGS sentence from Chemingui et al. (AAAI 2024) 'Summary and Future Work': 'This perspective is aimed at improving the search strategy in offline BBO, which complements prior methods that have focused on improving surrogate models while using fixed search strategies.' The same note confirms by grep that PGS holds the surrogate fixed at a single MLP (0 hits for 'Gaussian process,' 'ensemble,' 'ANOVA,' 'factorial') and varies only the RL search policy.
findings.recommendation: Insert the verbatim PGS premise sentence into the candidate A paragraph (and optionally N6) as the exact claim candidate A falsifies, paired with the grep fact that PGS varies only the search policy. This converts A's ownership claim from paraphrase to the sentence-level evidence the query demands.

findings.location: N5 section ('NTK / Spectral Bias and the Finite-Width Objection', ~lines 57-61), where the draft names Jacot [14], Lee-2018 [29], Rahaman [30] and states the objection is 'neither evidenced by the K-sweep nor fatal.'
findings.issue: The draft omits the single newly-fetched primary source the interim ran specifically to answer the finite-width objection, and it states the paper's per-member width (96) without engaging the scope consequence that 96 sits far below the NTK-agreement regime. This makes N5 read as more cleanly resolved for candidate D than the interim's own medium (65%) confidence warrants.
findings.evidence: interim-report-k-and-finite-width-artifact-vs-class-property fetched Lee, Xiao, Schoenholz et al., 'Wide Neural Networks of Any Depth Evolve as Linear Models Under Gradient Descent' (NeurIPS 2019, arXiv:1902.06720): 'GPs still outperform trained neural networks for both small and large dataset size' even as width grows toward the infinite limit; the finite/infinite-width gap is 'highly architecture-dependent' and an 'open research question.' The same note flags that width < 100 (the draft states hidden width 96) is far below Lee's n>=512-2048 NTK-agreement widths, so a genuine width-driven component 'cannot be ruled out -- it just isn't evidenced by the K-sweep specifically.'
findings.recommendation: Add Lee 2019 (arXiv:1902.06720) with the 'GPs still outperform ... both small and large dataset size' quote as literature-grounded support that width does not rescue the ensemble in the small-data regime, and add the scope caveat that the paper's width 96 << 512-2048 keeps the finite-width objection genuinely alive (so N5's PARTIAL should be stated with the interim's medium confidence, not as fully answered).

findings.location: N3 section ('Unmatched Effective Pessimism', ~lines 45-47), which defends the offline-MBO-acquisition NONE-FOUND residual using only Dewolf [11], Ghasemipour [23], and Srinivas [24].
findings.issue: The NONE-FOUND residual is asserted without the two nearest adversarial candidates the interim fetched full-text and ruled out. For an audit whose method requirement is 'at least one adversarial search per claim' and 'FETCH PRIMARY AND GREP IT,' dropping the two papers most likely to be a counterexample weakens the residual and hides the adversarial work already paid for.
findings.evidence: interim-report-n3-classic-bo-beta-calibration fetched and grepped two adversarial candidates: (1) Lu, Polyzos, Li, Giannakis, 'Surrogate modeling for Bayesian optimization beyond a single Gaussian process' (TPAMI 2023, arXiv:2205.14090) -- sidesteps beta via Thompson sampling over an ensemble of GPs ('requires no additional design parameters'; 0 hits for 'beta,' 'different surrogate,' 'sigma'); (2) Benechehab, Thomas, Kegl (arXiv:2402.02858) -- compares bootstrap ensembles vs autoregressive density nets with 24 'calibrat' hits, but aims to REPLACE the worse-calibrated class, never diagnosing that a SHARED coefficient produces mismatched effective conservatism from sigma-scale differences.
findings.recommendation: Add one or two sentences to N3 naming Lu et al. (2023) and Benechehab et al. (2024) as the nearest adversarial candidates checked and ruled out (the field's instinct is to fuse or replace surrogate classes, never to hold one nominal beta fixed across classes and diagnose the conservatism mismatch), so the NONE-FOUND residual is shown to survive a targeted adversarial sweep.

findings.location: N7 section ('Bidirectional Smoothness Manipulation', ~lines 82-84), which supports the 'NONE FOUND, first at all' verdict with Lim [17], IGNITE [18], and ROOT [36].
findings.issue: N7 is the paper's highest-ceiling 'first at all' claim across the entire BO/kernel-methods literature, yet the draft omits the closest LEXICAL counterexample the interim fetched -- a method that explicitly pools rougher AND smoother GPs, which a reviewer searching 'vary smoothness' would surface first and read as a potential counterexample.
findings.evidence: interim-report-n7-roughening-beyond-offline-mbo fetched and grepped Ziomek, Adachi & Osborne, 'Bayesian Optimisation with Unknown Hyperparameters: Regret Bounds Logarithmically Closer to Optimal' (arXiv:2410.10384). Its Length-scale Balancing method 'aggregat[es] multiple base surrogate models with varying length scales' (adds rougher candidates while retaining smoother ones) -- the closest lexical match to bidirectional smoothness manipulation found in the sweep -- but is ruled out: full-text grep for 'neural network' returns exactly one unrelated hit, every base model is a GP, there is no cross-surrogate-class comparison and no attribution of a between-class gap to smoothness.
findings.recommendation: Add Ziomek/Length-scale Balancing (arXiv:2410.10384) to N7 as the nearest lexical near-miss, explicitly ruled out (all-GP pool, no NN arm, no cross-class causal attribution). This pre-empts the counterexample most likely to be raised against the strongest 'first at all' claim in the paper.

findings.location: N9 section ('The De-Confounding Direction', ~line 95), the Recht partial: 'the model-to-model relative-gain slope exceeds 1'.
findings.issue: The draft conveys Recht's slope>1 qualitatively but omits the specific slope magnitudes the interim recorded, leaving the 'relative slope vs. variance-explained scalar' distinction less concrete than the interim supports.
findings.evidence: interim-report-audit-strengthens-and-n9-integrity records Recht's fitted slope of new-test vs original-test accuracy as 1.69 on CIFAR-10 and 1.11 on ImageNet, alongside 'the opposite of the standard overfitting scenario' and 'an increased advantage over earlier models.'
findings.recommendation: Add the slope numbers (1.69 CIFAR-10, 1.11 ImageNet) to the Recht partial so the reader sees exactly why it is a relative model-ranking slope, not an audited scalar effect-size statistic exceeding its own published value.

findings.location: N5 verdict-table cell (~line 19, 'Li/Rudner/Wilson App. D.1.2 [8]') and 'Three Strongest Rejecting Citations' #1 (~line 122, 'shows the ranking invariant to architecture size in Appendix D.1.2').
findings.issue: The draft twice attributes L/R/W's architecture-size / finite-width answer to 'Appendix D.1.2,' but the source interim note locates the relevant basin-of-attraction mechanism and architecture-size material in Appendix D.3 (and the 'minimal effects' sensitivity result in Sec. 4.1). The appendix pointer the audit hands a reviewer should match the source.
findings.evidence: interim-report-k-and-finite-width-artifact-vs-class-property quotes the 'even with the smaller architecture ... the relative performance of the surrogate models mostly remains consistent' result and the 'fewer settings of parameters that give rise to easily discoverable basins of attraction' mechanism from 'Appendix D.3, Fig. A.6 caption and surrounding text,' and the 'these hyperparameters generally have minimal effects on the performance' finding from 'Sec. 4.1' -- it never cites D.1.2.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile the appendix pointer against the source note (use Appendix D.3 / Sec. 4.1 as the interim documents), or verify D.1.2 directly in L/R/W before asserting it, so the location the audit cites is defensible.
